newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson - early payments lift cash flow.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson - early payments lift cash flow.

text.p: Swedish telecommunications group AB LM Ericsson said on Tuesday strong profits, quick deliveries and unexpected early customer payments were behind a strong order intake in the fourth quarter.
"The fourth quarter was a very good quarter profit-wise and deliveries flowed quite well...We have decreased our stockpiles," Ericsson deputy managing director C W Ros told Reuters.
"In addition we have received payments from a few major customers that we did not expect until the first quarter," he said after a news conference in connection with the company's 1996 results.
He said said these three factors accounted for most of the positive cash flow in 1996.
"It was perhaps the difference between a break-even level and four billion crowns," he said.
Ericsson posted a positive cash flow of four billion crowns for 1996.
Ros would not give a profit forecast for 1997 but regarding cash flow he said the company hoped to maintain the positive development of operating capital.
The early customer payments during the fourth quarter of 1996 could, however, be expected to affect the first quarter in 1997.
He would not say if Ericsson counted on positive cash flows from now on. This would instead depend on the company's rate of expansion.
Ros said that part of the provisions that had been made in the 1996 result for changes in technology and increased financial exposure could be regained.
"We think we that we have covered all the risks there are. Some of them can absolutely be taken back," Ros said.
